title: The frontend refuses to let a trader continue while any document is still being scanned, and offers a manual refresh link; DR1 lets them continue and finishes the check by itself.

finding.frontend: Pressing Continue while any document's scan is unsettled re-renders the page with the summary error "You cannot continue until all documents have been scanned or removed" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/scan/summary-errors.js:21-24, fired from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:272-277); a document whose scan came back rejected is named instead, file by file. While a scan is pending the page also offers a "Refresh virus scan status" link for traders without JavaScript, and a hidden timeout line reading "Still checking some documents. Refresh again in a moment." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:82-87). Neither captured frontend state is mid-scan, so this is read from source.
finding.prototype: DR1's continue path has no scan check at all: it validates the add form when a document type has been chosen, saves, and moves on regardless of what any row's tag says (app/routes.js:10174-10193). dr1-upload-documents-populated-scanning shows a document tagged "Scanning for virus" with Save and continue live beside it and no error, and dr1-upload-documents-limit-error shows fifteen rows all mid-scan on a page whose only complaint is the file count. There is no refresh control anywhere; the tag settles on its own.
finding.difference: What is not in doubt is the difference: a frontend trader is held on the page until every scan settles, a DR1 trader is not. What cannot be settled from the evidence is whether DR1 is stating a requirement or simply not modelling one. Its virus check is a fiction — a browser-side timer posts to a stub endpoint after a fixed delay and flips the row to passed, and no path in the prototype can ever produce a failed check (app/routes.js:9026 and 10124-10132) — so a design that never has a failure to catch would not need a gate whether or not the real service does. Settle it with a designer: if a real submission must not carry an unscanned or infected attachment, the frontend's gate is right and DR1 is silent rather than contrary, and this finding should be struck. If a trader is meant to be able to continue and be told later, the gate and the refresh link both come out. One fact sharpens the question for whoever settles it: the frontend's gate is not a rule about submission, it is a rule about one button. It is skipped whenever the trader leaves by "Save and return to hub", so an unsettled scan can already be walked past today — the gate delays the trader on this page rather than keeping an unscanned attachment out of a notification. If the intent is the latter, the check belongs on the submission path, not on Continue.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding any statement in DR1 — on the page, in the hub, or on the check-answers page — that a notification may be submitted while a document is still being scanned, or that it may not.
finding.verification: The band and the reasoning behind it both hold, and I tried to break the reasoning rather than read it. DR1's virus status takes exactly two values in the whole prototype: documents are created with virusStatus: 'uploading' (routes.js:9167) and the only writer anywhere is markUploadedDocumentVirusCheckPassed, which sets 'passed' and nothing else (:9172-9176); it is reached only from the stub endpoint at :10124-10132, driven by a browser timer of VIRUS_CHECK_DELAY_MS = 2500 (:9026, and app/assets/javascripts/upload-documents-virus-check.js:5,19,44). A grep for virusStatus across routes.js returns no third state and no failure path, so the author's premise — that DR1 has no failure to catch and its silence may be prototype fidelity rather than a requirement — is sound, and disputed is the honest band. The frontend half checks out too: settlingSummaryErrors returns the cannotContinue message only when nothing is REJECTED and rejectedErrors names files individually otherwise (scan/summary-errors.js:11-24, prepended on every render at view-model/render.js:30-34), fired from controller.js:273-277; the "for traders without JavaScript" characterisation of the refresh link is right, since the client hides #js-refresh-fallback as soon as polling starts (client/scan-status/poll.js:57-70). DR1's continue branch at routes.js:10173-10193 reads no scan status, and the scanning screenshot shows Save and continue live beside a "Scanning for virus" row with no error. One sentence added to the difference slot, see correction.
finding.correction: No claim fell; the dispute was stated correctly but not completely enough to be settled. The finding described the gate as though it governed whether a notification may carry an unscanned attachment, which is the question it asks a designer to answer. It does not: controller.js:273 guards the check with !kit.hubExitTarget(request), so pressing "Save and return to hub" leaves the page with an unsettled scan and no error. A sentence recording that has been added to the difference slot, because it changes the answer — the choice is not "gate or no gate" but "is this check on the right button", and a designer cannot rule on it without knowing the exit already bypasses it.
